topics.concept: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium predicts genotype frequencies p^2, 2pq, q^2 from allele frequencies under random mating with no selection, mutation, or drift. A chi-square test of observed versus expected counts detects violations. The tester reports allele frequencies, expected counts, and the equilibrium verdict.
topics.data_idea: The demo draws seeded-RNG random genotypes from known allele frequencies and checks the tester accepts equilibrium.
topics.name: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium Tester
topics.real_world_use: HWE testing QC's genotyping data and detects selection or stratification in GWAS.

topics.concept: Mendel's ratios (3:1, 9:3:3:1, 1:1) are hypotheses tested with chi-square: squared deviations of observed from expected counts, scaled by expectation. The analyzer takes observed offspring counts and a hypothesized ratio, returning the statistic, p-value, and accept/reject verdict. It warns when expected counts are too small.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random offspring from known ratios and checks acceptance rates.
topics.name: Mendelian Ratio Chi-Square Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Ratio testing validates inheritance patterns in breeding and genetics labs.

topics.concept: A Punnett square enumerates all gamete combinations from two parents, giving offspring genotype and phenotype probabilities for single-gene traits. The simulator generalizes to any parental genotypes and dominance schemes, including incomplete dominance and codominance. It draws the square and summarizes probabilities.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random crosses and verifies offspring frequencies match the square's predictions.
topics.name: Punnett Square Cross Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Punnett squares teach inheritance and predict breeding outcomes in agriculture.

topics.concept: Dihybrid crosses track two genes at once: independent assortment gives the 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio, while linkage distorts it toward parental types. The analyzer computes expected offspring distributions under both hypotheses and fits recombination fractions. It reports which model the data support.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random dihybrid offspring under known linkage and checks the analyzer recovers the recombination fraction.
topics.name: Dihybrid Cross Linkage Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Dihybrid analysis maps genes in model-organism genetics.

topics.concept: Recombination frequency between two loci estimates their map distance: 1 percent recombination equals 1 centimorgan (with mapping-function corrections for double crossovers). The mapper takes testcross offspring counts, computes recombinant fractions, and converts to map distances via Haldane or Kosambi functions. It orders multiple loci by pairwise distances.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random testcross data from known map distances and checks recovery.
topics.name: Recombination Frequency Map Builder
topics.real_world_use: Linkage mapping locates genes in breeding programs and model organisms.

topics.concept: Autosomal dominant traits appear every generation with 50 percent transmission from an affected heterozygote; recessive traits skip generations and cluster in consanguineous families. The pedigree analyzer scores a pedigree against dominant, recessive, and X-linked models, ruling out incompatible ones. It explains each ruling with the violated expectation.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random pedigrees under known inheritance modes and checks the analyzer identifies them.
topics.name: Autosomal Pedigree Mode Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Pedigree analysis is the first step in clinical genetics consultations.

topics.concept: X-linked traits show criss-cross inheritance: fathers pass X to daughters only, so affected fathers have carrier daughters and affected sons inherit from carrier mothers. The solver computes transmission probabilities through a pedigree and flags obligate carriers. It handles X-linked dominant and recessive separately.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random X-linked pedigrees and verifies computed carrier probabilities.
topics.name: X-Linked Pedigree Solver
topics.real_world_use: X-linked analysis counsels families for conditions like hemophilia and color blindness.

topics.concept: The Wright-Fisher model samples 2N gene copies each generation from the previous one, so allele frequencies wander by drift with variance p(1-p)/2N per generation. Small populations fix or lose alleles quickly. The simulator tracks allele trajectories, time to fixation, and heterozygosity decay.
topics.data_idea: The demo runs seeded-RNG random replicate populations and checks fixation times match diffusion approximations.
topics.name: Wright-Fisher Drift Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Drift models explain allele loss in endangered species and lab evolution.

topics.concept: A selection coefficient s changes allele fitnesses (1, 1+hs, 1+s), driving deterministic frequency change layered over drift. The simulator integrates the deterministic recursion and adds binomial sampling noise for finite populations. It reports time to fixation and the probability of fixation from a single copy.
topics.data_idea: The demo runs seeded-RNG random selection trajectories and compares fixation probabilities to the 2s approximation.
topics.name: Selection Coefficient Trajectory Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Selection models predict pesticide resistance and antibiotic resistance spread.

topics.concept: Deleterious alleles persist at mutation-selection balance: new mutations arrive at rate mu while selection removes them, equilibrating near mu/s for dominant alleles. The calculator derives equilibrium frequencies for dominant, recessive, and overdominant cases. It shows how recessives hide at higher frequencies.
topics.data_idea: The demo iterates seeded-RNG random mutation-selection recursions and checks convergence to the predicted equilibria.
topics.name: Mutation-Selection Balance Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Balance theory explains why harmful alleles persist in human populations.

topics.concept: The island model connects subpopulations by migration at rate m per generation, which homogenizes allele frequencies and opposes drift-driven divergence. Equilibrium Fst approximates 1/(1+4Nm). The simulator runs multiple demes with migration and tracks divergence over time.
topics.data_idea: The demo runs seeded-RNG random multi-deme simulations and checks Fst converges near the theoretical value.
topics.name: Island Model Migration Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Migration models guide wildlife corridor design and interpret human population structure.

topics.concept: The coalescent traces gene copies backward in time: pairs merge at rate depending on population size, and mutations fall on branches as a Poisson process. Simulating genealogies this way is far cheaper than forward simulation. The tool generates trees, overlays mutations, and reports pairwise diversity.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random coalescent trees and checks pairwise differences match the theta expectation.
topics.name: Coalescent Genealogy Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Coalescent methods infer demographic history from DNA samples in human genetics.

topics.concept: Effective population size Ne is the size of an ideal population experiencing the same drift as the real one; it is reduced by skewed sex ratios, variance in offspring number, and bottlenecks. The estimator computes Ne from demographic inputs via the harmonic-mean and sex-ratio formulas. It contrasts Ne with census size.
topics.data_idea: The demo computes Ne for seeded-RNG random demographic scenarios and checks the harmonic-mean behavior.
topics.name: Effective Population Size Estimator
topics.real_world_use: Ne estimates assess extinction risk in conservation biology.

topics.concept: The inbreeding coefficient F is the probability that two alleles in an individual are identical by descent; it rises with consanguineous mating and small population size. The calculator derives F from pedigree loops or from heterozygote deficiency. It predicts the increased risk of recessive disorders.
topics.data_idea: The demo computes F for seeded-RNG random pedigrees and validates against path-method calculations.
topics.name: Inbreeding Coefficient Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Inbreeding estimates manage zoo breeding and livestock programs.

topics.concept: Wright's path method computes inbreeding by summing (1/2)^n over every path connecting the parents through a common ancestor, where n counts individuals in the path. The tool enumerates all such paths in a pedigree graph and sums their contributions. It handles multiple common ancestors.
topics.data_idea: The demo evaluates seeded-RNG random pedigrees and cross-checks path sums against matrix-method F.
topics.name: Pedigree Path-Method Inbreeding Tool
topics.real_world_use: Path analysis quantifies inbreeding in royal, isolated, and pedigree dog populations.

topics.concept: QTL mapping crosses divergent lines and tests each genomic position for association with a quantitative trait; LOD-like scores peak near causal loci. The simulator generates a cross with planted QTLs of known effect, runs interval mapping, and reports detected peaks versus truth. It demonstrates the Beavis effect of overestimated small effects.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random crosses with planted QTLs and measures detection power by effect size.
topics.name: QTL Interval Mapping Simulator
topics.real_world_use: QTL mapping finds crop-yield and disease-resistance genes in breeding programs.

topics.concept: A Manhattan plot stacks association p-values across the genome; true signals tower above the noise as skyscraper peaks. The simulator plants causal variants with realistic effect sizes, runs association tests with population-structure noise, and renders the plot data with a genome-wide significance line. It reports power and false-positive rates.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random GWAS panels with planted signals and checks peak detection.
topics.name: GWAS Manhattan Plot Simulator
topics.real_world_use: GWAS identifies disease-associated loci in human genetics.

topics.concept: Twin studies estimate heritability by comparing identical (MZ) and fraternal (DZ) twin correlations: Falconer's formula gives h^2 = 2(r_MZ - r_DZ). The ACE model further splits variance into additive genetic, shared, and unique environment. The estimator reports all components with confidence intervals.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random twin pairs with known variance components and checks recovery.
topics.name: Twin Study Heritability Estimator
topics.real_world_use: Heritability estimates partition nature versus nurture in behavioral genetics.

topics.concept: A polygenic score sums trait-increasing alleles weighted by their GWAS effect sizes, predicting individual genetic liability on a population scale. The calculator builds scores from genotype dosages and effect weights, then reports the score distribution and top-decile enrichment. It stresses that scores are probabilistic, not diagnostic.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random genotypes with known architectures and checks score-trait correlations.
topics.name: Polygenic Score Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Polygenic scores stratify risk in research biobanks (population-level, not clinical diagnosis).

topics.concept: Epistasis means one gene masks or modifies another, producing ratios like 9:7 (complementary), 12:3:1 (dominant epistasis), or 9:3:4 (recessive epistasis) instead of 9:3:3:1. The simulator generates offspring under each epistatic model and fits observed counts to identify the interaction type. It explains the deviating phenotypic classes.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random offspring under each epistasis model and checks model identification.
topics.name: Epistasis Ratio Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Epistasis analysis dissects interacting pathways in model-organism genetics.

topics.concept: The complementation test crosses two recessive mutants: if offspring are wild-type, the mutations are in different genes; if mutant, they are alleles of the same gene. The logic tool takes cross outcomes across mutant pairs and clusters them into complementation groups (genes). It handles incomplete outcomes gracefully.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random mutant panels with known gene assignments and checks group recovery.
topics.name: Complementation Test Logic Engine
topics.real_world_use: Complementation groups defined genes before sequencing in classical genetics.

topics.concept: Trihybrid crosses track three genes; with independent assortment the phenotypic ratio is 27:9:9:9:3:3:3:1. The predictor enumerates all 64 gamete combinations from parental genotypes and aggregates offspring genotype and phenotype probabilities. It flags linked gene pairs that would distort the ratio.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random trihybrid offspring and verifies frequencies match the predicted distribution.
topics.name: Trihybrid Cross Predictor
topics.real_world_use: Trihybrid prediction plans multi-trait breeding in crops and livestock.

topics.concept: Sex-linked transmission probabilities follow from X/Y segregation: a carrier mother passes the trait to half her sons, an affected father to none of his sons but all daughters become carriers. The calculator propagates these probabilities through arbitrary pedigrees. It reports each individual's carrier and affected probabilities.
topics.data_idea: The demo evaluates seeded-RNG random pedigrees and validates probabilities against exact enumeration.
topics.name: Sex-Linkage Probability Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Risk calculation counsels families about X-linked disorder transmission.

topics.concept: Pedigree risk calculation combines Mendelian transmission probabilities with observed family data via Bayes' rule to update carrier risks. Each new birth or test result revises the probabilities. The calculator processes pedigrees sequentially and reports posterior risks per individual.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random pedigrees with known carrier states and checks posterior calibration.
topics.name: Bayesian Pedigree Risk Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Bayesian risk updates are the quantitative core of genetic counseling.

topics.concept: A founder effect occurs when a new population starts from a few individuals, so its allele frequencies are a small random sample of the source, often losing rare alleles entirely. The simulator draws founder samples and tracks diversity loss over subsequent generations. It compares heterozygosity in founders versus source.
topics.data_idea: The demo draws seeded-RNG random founder samples and measures allele-loss rates by founder count.
topics.name: Founder Effect Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Founder effects explain disease alleles in island and isolate populations.

topics.concept: A population bottleneck crashes to a small size for a few generations, purging rare alleles and inflating drift; heterozygosity recovers slowly afterward. The simulator models the crash and recovery, tracking allele counts and heterozygosity. It contrasts bottlenecked versus stable control populations.
topics.data_idea: The demo runs seeded-RNG random bottleneck scenarios and checks heterozygosity loss against theoretical expectations.
topics.name: Population Bottleneck Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Bottleneck models interpret cheetah and elephant-seal genetic uniformity.

topics.concept: Assortative mating pairs similar phenotypes, increasing homozygosity and the variance of polygenic traits without changing allele frequencies. The model iterates genotype frequencies under positive assortative mating and tracks heterozygote decline. It contrasts with random and disassortative mating.
topics.data_idea: The demo iterates seeded-RNG random mating tables and verifies heterozygosity declines under assortative mating.
topics.name: Assortative Mating Model
topics.real_world_use: Assortative mating models human height and IQ partner correlations in quantitative genetics.

topics.concept: Overdominance (heterozygote advantage) maintains both alleles at a stable interior equilibrium p = s2/(s1+s2), where s1 and s2 are the homozygote disadvantages. The classic example is sickle-cell versus malaria. The calculator derives the equilibrium and simulates approach from any starting frequency.
topics.data_idea: The demo iterates seeded-RNG random overdominant systems and checks convergence to the predicted equilibrium.
topics.name: Overdominance Equilibrium Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Balancing selection explains MHC diversity and blood-group polymorphisms.

topics.concept: Balancing selection, through heterozygote advantage or frequency-dependent selection, actively maintains polymorphism against drift and directional selection. The simulator combines selection regimes with drift and reports equilibrium diversity versus neutral expectations. It detects the elevated heterozygosity signature.
topics.data_idea: The demo runs seeded-RNG random selection-plus-drift scenarios and compares diversity to neutral controls.
topics.name: Balancing Selection Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Balancing selection maintains immune-system diversity studied in evolutionary medicine.

topics.concept: Mitochondrial DNA passes only from mother to offspring, so pedigrees show strictly maternal transmission with all children of an affected mother inheriting the variant. The simulator traces mitochondrial haplotypes through pedigrees and flags paternal-transmission claims as errors. It models heteroplasmy thresholds for phenotype expression.
topics.data_idea: The demo traces seeded-RNG random mitochondrial variants through pedigrees and verifies maternal-only transmission.
topics.name: Mitochondrial Inheritance Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Maternal inheritance patterns diagnose mitochondrial disorders in clinics.

topics.concept: Imprinted genes express only the paternal or maternal copy, so the same allele causes disease only when inherited from a specific parent. The pedigree model tracks parent-of-origin for each transmission and predicts affected status accordingly. It explains pedigrees that defy Mendelian expectations.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random imprinted pedigrees and checks the model predicts the parent-of-origin pattern.
topics.name: Genomic Imprinting Pedigree Model
topics.real_world_use: Imprinting explains Prader-Willi and Angelman syndrome inheritance.

topics.concept: Penetrance is the probability a genotype shows any phenotype; expressivity is how severely. The modeler combines genotype probabilities with penetrance values to predict family phenotype patterns. It fits penetrance estimates from pedigree data by maximum likelihood.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random families with known penetrance and checks the estimator recovers it.
topics.name: Penetrance and Expressivity Modeler
topics.real_world_use: Penetrance modeling refines risk estimates for BRCA and other variable traits.

topics.concept: The LOD score is the log10 likelihood ratio of linkage at recombination fraction theta versus no linkage; scores above 3 traditionally declare linkage. The calculator sums LOD contributions across families from phase-known or phase-unknown meioses. It scans theta to find the maximum LOD and its support interval.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random family data with known linkage and checks LOD peaks at the true theta.
topics.name: LOD Score Linkage Calculator
topics.real_world_use: LOD scores mapped Mendelian disease genes before the GWAS era.

topics.concept: Haplotype phasing assigns each heterozygous allele to its parental chromosome; with only genotypes, phasing is ambiguous and needs statistical methods. The simulator generates true haplotypes, masks phase, and tests a parsimony-based phaser's accuracy. It reports switch-error rates by marker density.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random haplotype pairs and measures phasing accuracy across densities.
topics.name: Haplotype Phasing Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Phasing enables allele-specific analysis in clinical and population genomics.

topics.concept: Recombination concentrates in hotspots, short regions with far higher crossover rates than background, shaped by PRDM9 binding in mammals. The model places crossovers with a hotspot-modulated rate along a chromosome and reports hotspot usage statistics. It compares observed versus uniform crossover spacing.
topics.data_idea: The demo places seeded-RNG random crossovers under hotspot models and checks enrichment statistics.
topics.name: Recombination Hotspot Model
topics.real_world_use: Hotspot maps improve imputation and interpret LD patterns in GWAS.

topics.concept: Copy number variants duplicate or delete genomic segments; tandem duplications arise by non-allelic homologous recombination between repeats. The simulator generates CNV events with size distributions from empirical studies and tracks copy-number state along a chromosome. It reports CNV counts by type and size class.
topics.data_idea: The demo synthesizes seeded-RNG random CNV catalogs and validates size-distribution statistics.
topics.name: Copy Number Variant Simulator
topics.real_world_use: CNV simulation benchmarks detection tools for clinical microarray and sequencing.

topics.concept: Reciprocal translocations swap chromosome arms; carriers produce alternate (balanced), adjacent-1, adjacent-2, and 3:1 segregation products, mostly unbalanced. The tool enumerates gamete types from a translocation configuration and computes the probability of viable balanced offspring. It explains each segregation pattern.
topics.data_idea: The demo enumerates seeded-RNG random translocation configurations and verifies gamete counts by segregation type.
topics.name: Translocation Segregation Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Segregation analysis counsels translocation carriers about miscarriage and offspring risks.

topics.concept: Nondisjunction is the failure of chromosomes to separate in meiosis, producing aneuploid gametes; its probability rises sharply with maternal age. The calculator combines age-specific nondisjunction rates with chromosome-specific data to estimate aneuploidy risk. It reports risks by chromosome and maternal age.
topics.data_idea: The demo computes seeded-RNG random age-risk curves and checks monotonic increase with age.
topics.name: Nondisjunction Risk Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Aneuploidy risk tables inform prenatal screening decisions (population statistics, not diagnosis).

topics.concept: Gene drives bias inheritance above 50 percent (e.g., CRISPR homing converts heterozygotes), spreading engineered alleles through populations even with fitness costs. The simulator models drive spread with conversion efficiency, resistance-allele formation, and fitness costs. It reports time to fixation and containment thresholds.
topics.data_idea: The demo runs seeded-RNG random drive releases and checks spread rates against deterministic predictions.
topics.name: Gene Drive Spread Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Gene-drive models evaluate malaria mosquito-control strategies (research modeling only).

topics.concept: CRISPR editing produces a spectrum of outcomes: precise homology-directed repair, error-prone indels from non-homologous end joining, and unedited alleles, with probabilities depending on guide efficiency and cell state. The educational simulator samples outcomes for a target site and reports the edit spectrum. It is a teaching model, not a design tool.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random editing experiments and checks outcome frequencies match the input probabilities.
topics.name: CRISPR Edit Outcome Simulator (Educational)
topics.real_world_use: Outcome models teach genome-editing concepts in classrooms and training.

topics.concept: The genetic code is degenerate: 61 codons encode 20 amino acids, with third-position wobble carrying most redundancy. The analyzer tabulates codon degeneracy per amino acid, computes the fraction of synonymous versus nonsynonymous single-base changes, and reports the code's error-minimization properties. It compares against randomized codes.
topics.data_idea: The demo analyzes the standard code table deterministically and compares robustness metrics to seeded-RNG random codes.
topics.name: Genetic Code Degeneracy Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Code analysis informs theories of code evolution and synthetic-code design.

topics.concept: Clonal inheritance passes the entire genome without recombination, so mutations accumulate along lineages and phylogenies are simple trees. The tracker simulates clonal expansion with neutral mutations and reconstructs lineage relationships. It contrasts diversity patterns with sexual populations.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random clonal expansions and checks tree reconstruction accuracy.
topics.name: Clonal Lineage Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Clonal tracking studies bacterial outbreaks and cancer evolution.

topics.concept: Lethal recessive alleles persist because heterozygotes are healthy; selection removes them only in homozygotes, giving equilibrium near sqrt(mu/s) for full lethals. The calculator derives equilibrium frequencies for lethal and sublethal alleles under dominance models. It shows why lethals are rarer than mild recessives.
topics.data_idea: The demo iterates seeded-RNG random lethal-allele systems and checks convergence to predicted equilibria.
topics.name: Lethal Allele Equilibrium Calculator
topics.real_world_use: Lethal-allele theory explains persistence of severe recessive disorders.

topics.concept: Mutation rates are estimated by fluctuation tests: parallel cultures show jackpot distributions because early mutations produce many descendants. The simulator grows cultures with stochastic mutations and fits the mutation rate from the mutant-count distribution using the Lea-Coulson approach. It contrasts with naive averaging.
topics.data_idea: The demo simulates seeded-RNG random fluctuation tests with known mutation rates and checks estimator accuracy.
topics.name: Fluctuation Test Mutation-Rate Estimator
topics.real_world_use: Fluctuation analysis measures mutation rates in microbiology and cancer biology.
